description: Defining, provisioning and maintaining infrastructure as version-controlled code: the case for automation, declarative provisioning with Terraform, reusable modules, state and drift, configuration management with Ansible, testing infrastructure, policy as code and GitOps workflows. Practised in simulated terminals and a simulated cloud console in the browser, where every plan and apply shows its effect on real-looking resources, taught to the depth of the infrastructure automation certifications.
modelledOn: Morris, Infrastructure as Code: Dynamic Systems for the Cloud Age
outcomes: Justify infrastructure as code by contrasting it with manual, ticket-driven provisioning and identify where it fails.
Write declarative Terraform configurations that provision networks, compute, storage and identity on a cloud platform.
Design reusable, versioned modules and structure code for multiple environments and teams.
Manage remote state safely, detect and reconcile drift, and import existing resources.
Configure servers idempotently with Ansible and choose between immutable and mutable infrastructure.
Test infrastructure code, enforce policy and deliver changes through GitOps workflows with review and audit.

units.title: Why infrastructure as code
topics: The problems of manual provisioning: snowflake servers, configuration drift, undocumented changes, slow recovery
Principles: everything in version control, idempotence, repeatability, disposability, small changes
Declarative versus imperative tools; provisioning versus configuration management; the tool landscape
Infrastructure as code in a team: code review for infrastructure, change records, blast radius

units.title: Declarative provisioning
topics: HCL syntax: providers, resources, data sources, variables, outputs, locals
The workflow: init, plan, apply, destroy; reading a plan; the dependency graph and parallelism
Expressions: count, for_each, conditionals, dynamic blocks, built-in functions
Provisioning a VPC, subnets, security groups, virtual machines and object storage
Cloud-native alternatives in brief: CloudFormation, Bicep, Pulumi and OpenTofu

units.title: Modules and reuse
topics: Writing modules: inputs, outputs, encapsulation; root and child modules
Module sources and versioning: registries, Git tags, semantic versioning
Composing modules into stacks; environment layouts for development, staging and production
Workspaces versus separate directories; managing differences with variable files
A reusable module for a three-tier web application used by several teams

units.title: State and drift
topics: What state is and why it exists: mapping configuration to real resources
Remote backends, state locking and encryption; secrets that leak into state
Drift: how it happens, detecting it with refresh and plan, deciding whether to revert or adopt
Refactoring safely: moved blocks, state mv, rm and import; splitting large states
Recovering from a corrupted or lost state file

units.title: Configuration management
topics: Ansible architecture: inventories, ad hoc commands, playbooks, modules, agentless SSH
Idempotent tasks, handlers, variables, facts and templates with Jinja2
Roles and collections; Ansible Vault for secrets
Immutable infrastructure: building golden images with Packer versus configuring running servers
Configuring a fleet of servers for a mobile money agent network, with Terraform and Ansible working together

units.title: Testing infrastructure
topics: The testing pyramid for infrastructure: formatting, validation, static analysis, unit, integration, end-to-end
Linting and security scanning: tflint, Checkov, tfsec; ansible-lint
Native terraform test, Terratest and Molecule; ephemeral test environments and their cost
Policy as code with Open Policy Agent and Sentinel: blocking public buckets and enforcing data residency rules
Cost estimation in pull requests

units.title: GitOps workflows
topics: GitOps principles: Git as the source of truth, declarative desired state, pull-based reconciliation
CI/CD for infrastructure: plan on pull request, apply on merge, approvals and protected environments
Argo CD and Flux for Kubernetes; Atlantis and similar tools for Terraform
Secrets in GitOps: sealed secrets, external secret operators, short-lived credentials with OIDC

units.title: Operating infrastructure as code at scale
topics: Disaster recovery by rebuilding from code; tested recovery times
Platform engineering and self-service infrastructure; golden paths
Compliance and audit: change history, tagging standards, data residency under the Data Protection Act
Capstone: provision, configure, test and deliver through GitOps a complete environment, then detect and fix injected drift

schedule.title: Why infrastructure as code
schedule.exercise: Write a short account of a server that nobody dares to touch, naming the manual steps that caused it and how code would have prevented each.

tasks.title: Build a web server by hand in the cloud console, document every click, then destroy it and time how long a rebuild takes
Show that a provisioning script is idempotent by running it three times and checking that the second and third runs change nothing
Review a risky infrastructure change request with a large blast radius, decide what to approve, split or reject, and justify against a rubric

schedule.title: Terraform fundamentals
schedule.exercise: Read a given plan output line by line and explain what will be created, changed or destroyed and why.

tasks.title: Write a configuration with a provider, one virtual machine, a variable and an output, then run init, plan and apply
Read a plan that shows a resource replacement, find the argument that forces it, and change the code to update it in place
Use for_each, a conditional and a dynamic block to create security group rules for three environments from a single variable map

schedule.title: Provisioning networks and servers
schedule.exercise: Draw the network diagram for a two-subnet web and database environment and label every security group rule with its purpose.

tasks.title: Provision a VPC with one public subnet and one virtual machine, and confirm the machine is reachable only on port 80
Provision a VPC with public and private subnets, a database server and an object storage bucket with restricted access, then test the paths
Express the same small environment in Terraform and in a cloud-native template, compare readability and drift handling, and write the trade-offs

schedule.title: Modules and composition
schedule.exercise: Write the interface documentation of a module, listing every input, output and default, and one example call.

tasks.title: Turn a repeated virtual machine definition into a module with inputs and outputs and call it twice with different names
Version a module with Git tags following semantic versioning, upgrade a caller to a new minor version, and read the plan for surprises
Compose network, compute and database modules into a stack with separate development, staging and production layouts that differ only by variables

schedule.title: Environments and reusable modules
schedule.exercise: Compare workspaces with separate directories for three environments, listing the risk each approach carries.

tasks.title: Create development and production variable files for the same configuration and apply each, comparing the resources created
Switch between two workspaces, show the state is separate for each, and describe the mistake that applying to the wrong workspace would cause
Design a reusable three-tier web application module with load balancer, autoscaling group and database, used by two teams with different sizes

schedule.title: State and drift
schedule.exercise: Explain in a paragraph why state files may contain secrets and list three controls that reduce the risk.

tasks.title: Inspect a state file from a small deployment and match each resource entry to the real resource it records
Move state to a remote backend with locking, run two applies at the same time, and show that the lock stops the second
Change a security group by hand in the console, detect the drift with a plan, and decide whether to revert the change or adopt it into code

schedule.title: Refactoring state and recovery
schedule.exercise: Write a recovery runbook for a lost state file, listing the steps in order and the checks that prove the rebuilt state is correct.

tasks.title: Rename a resource using a moved block and show in the plan that nothing will be destroyed or recreated
Import two existing console-created resources into state, write matching code, and reach a plan with no changes
Recover from a deleted state file by importing every resource of a three-tier stack, then verify with a clean plan and record the recovery time

schedule.title: Configuration management with Ansible
schedule.exercise: Write a playbook outline for a web server setup, marking each task and handler and explaining why each is safe to run repeatedly.

tasks.title: Write an inventory and run an ad hoc command to check disk space and uptime on three virtual machines
Write a playbook that installs a web server, templates its configuration with Jinja2 and restarts it only through a handler when the file changes
Refactor a playbook into a role, move the database password into Ansible Vault, and show that the playbook runs idempotently

schedule.title: Immutable images and combined workflows
schedule.exercise: Argue in writing whether a fleet of 50 mobile money agent servers should be patched in place or rebuilt from images, with costs and risks.

tasks.title: Build a golden image from a base machine with the web server installed and launch two identical instances from it
Provision five servers with Terraform and configure them with Ansible, then show a re-run produces no changes
Roll out a configuration change to a fleet of 20 servers in batches, with a health check that halts the rollout when a batch fails

schedule.title: Testing infrastructure code
schedule.exercise: Place ten checks of your own project on the testing pyramid and say how long each takes and what bug class it catches.

tasks.title: Run format, validate and a linter on a configuration with three planted errors and fix each one until all checks pass
Run a security scanner on a stack with an open storage bucket and an open admin port, then fix each finding and re-scan
Write integration tests that create an ephemeral environment, check that it serves a page and then destroy it, and estimate the cost per run

schedule.title: Policy as code and cost control
schedule.exercise: Write three policies in plain words for a bank's cloud account, then say which could be automated as code and which could not.

tasks.title: Write a policy that blocks any public storage bucket and show a plan that violates it being rejected before apply
Add a data residency policy that allows resources only in approved regions and test it with one compliant and one non-compliant plan
Estimate the monthly cost of a pull request that adds autoscaling, set a budget threshold, and decide when the change needs approval

schedule.title: GitOps and pipelines
schedule.exercise: Draw the pipeline from pull request to production for infrastructure, marking the human approvals, the automated checks and what each blocks.

tasks.title: Keep a configuration in a Git repository, make a change by pull request, and show the history that explains who changed what and why
Build a pipeline that runs plan on pull request and apply on merge to main, with a protected production environment requiring approval
Replace a long-lived cloud key in a pipeline with short-lived credentials from OIDC, and show that a leaked token expires and cannot be reused

schedule.title: Recovery, platforms and capstone
schedule.exercise: Capstone report: describe the environment you built, the tests and pipeline you used, the injected drift you found and how you fixed it.

tasks.title: Destroy a complete test environment and rebuild it from code, recording the time taken and the manual steps still needed
Add required tags and region rules to a stack, run a compliance check, and produce a change history report for an auditor
Provision, configure and deliver a full environment through a pipeline, then detect and fix three drift items planted by the examiner
